# Threat Model — OWASP Juice Shop v20.2.0 (http://host.docker.internal:3001)

## Overview
Deliberately vulnerable training application (OWASP Juice Shop v20.2.0), a Node.js/Express + Sequelize backend with an Angular SPA frontend, deployed locally and authorized for full security validation. Everything on this host is product/runtime surface: REST API (`/rest/*`), Sequelize-backed JSON API (`/api/*`), file directories (`/ftp`, `/3d`), an LLM chatbot (`/rest/chat`), and web3/NFT endpoints. Swagger UI at `/api-docs/`. This is a test instance with seeded demo data, so findings are rated for the vulnerability class they demonstrate, not for real-user data harm.

## Trust Boundaries and Assumptions
- **Unauthenticated internet user** — the baseline attacker. Can reach: login, registration, product search, `/api/Products`, `/api/Feedbacks` GET, track-order, security-question lookup, `/redirect?to=`, `/ftp` directory listings, `/metrics`, and (notably) `GET /rest/admin/application-configuration` and `/rest/admin/application-version`.
- **Authenticated customer** — any registered account (recon test account: `tester.recon@juice-sh.op` / `recon123456`, id=25, basket id=6; JWT saved at `/workspace/recon_token.txt`). Can reach baskets, wallet, orders, feedback, reviews, complaints, addresses, cards, data erasure, 2FA, chatbot.
- **Deluxe member** — additional coupon/offer surfaces via `/rest/deluxe-membership`.
- **Admin** — `/rest/admin`, product PUT, order delivery status, accounting. The Angular `administration` route guard is **client-side only**; the server is expected to enforce role via JWT claims — this is the key boundary to test.
- **Token model**: `POST /rest/user/login` issues an **RS256 JWT with no `exp` claim** whose payload embeds the full user record (including password hash and `totpSecret`). Token honored as `Authorization: Bearer` and as a `token` cookie (whoami requires the cookie). Signature verification quality, algorithm confusion, and the missing-exp issue are prime targets.
- **Inferred, not observed**: whether the JWT public key is retrievable (main.js bundle, exposed config) — needs verification by the auth specialist.

## Attack Surface and Attacker Stories
- **Injection**: `POST /rest/user/login` (classic SQLi), `GET /rest/products/search?q=`, `POST /rest/track-order` (Sequelize/SQLite stack; error pages leak stack traces).
- **Broken access control / IDOR**: `GET /rest/basket/:id` (server compares to token `bid` — test other ids), `/api/Addresss/:id`, `/api/Cards/:id`, `/api/Users/:id`, `/rest/order-history`, `POST /rest/admin` with forged role claims.
- **AuthN/AuthZ**: JWT forgery (alg none/confusion, weak or exposed key material), missing token expiry, mass-assignment of `role` at `POST /api/Users`, password reset flow (`/rest/user/security-question?email=` enumeration + reset), 2FA bypass with `totpSecret` leaked in token payload, `change-password` via query-string parameters.
- **XSS**: reflected via search DOM rendering, stored via feedback comments, product reviews, photo-wall memories.
- **SSRF / open redirect**: `GET /redirect?to=` (URL allowlist present — bypass candidate), data-erasure and profile-image URL features, LLM chatbot tool calls.
- **Sensitive exposure**: `/ftp` listing (kdbx, `.bak`, `encrypt.pyc`), `package.json.bak`, unauth full config dump at `/rest/admin/application-configuration`, `/metrics`.
- **Business logic**: wallet balance PUT, expired coupons from `/ftp/coupons_2013.md.bak`, negative quantities at checkout, product price tampering, deluxe membership race.
- **Not realistic here**: attacks on other hosts/services on the docker network beyond demonstrating SSRF reachability; real-user data harm (demo data only).

## Severity Calibration
- **Critical**: unauthenticated auth bypass / admin access via forged or forged-claim JWT; RCE-class issues; unauthenticated mass data disclosure (e.g., full config with secrets).
- **High**: SQLi reaching the database, IDOR exposing other users' data or modifying other users' baskets, stored XSS executing for other users, JWT forgery requiring exposed key material.
- **Medium**: stored XSS in limited context, open redirect with allowlist bypass, wallet/coupon logic abuse, information disclosure materially aiding attacks.
- **Low/Info**: missing headers, verbose errors, enumeration-only issues.
- Because this is a deliberately vulnerable demo app with seeded data, impact is scored on the demonstrated consequence class, and business-context deductions are noted in report assumptions.

amendments.content:
## Amendment — Broken access control results (IDOR specialist)

The base model flagged `/rest/basket/:id`, `/api/Addresss/:id`, `/api/Cards/:id`, `/api/Users/:id`, `/rest/order-history` and `POST /rest/admin` as IDOR/BFLA candidates. Verified results:

- **Confirmed cross-user access (reported)**: `GET /rest/basket/:id` (read any basket), `POST /rest/basket/:id/checkout` (empty another user's basket, order created in attacker's account), `PUT/DELETE /api/Addresss/:id` (modify/delete another user's address; PUT also reassigns UserId to caller), `GET /api/Users` + `/api/Users/:id` (full user directory incl. admin email to any customer), `GET /api/Complaints` (all users' complaints), `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/BasketItems(:id)` (read/modify/delete other users' items; POST correctly guarded).
- **Enforced (ruled out)**: `/api/Cards/:id` all methods, per-object `GET /api/Addresss/:id`, `PUT /api/Users/:id`, `/api/SecurityAnswers`, and admin function-level routes `GET /rest/order-history/orders` + `PUT /rest/order-history/:id/delivery-status` (403 "Malicious activity detected" for customer tokens — server-side role enforcement DOES exist). `PUT /rest/products/:id` and `POST /rest/admin` are not registered routes in this build (500 "Unexpected path").
- **Severity calibration note**: cross-user basket read/checkout and user-directory disclosure are Medium; cross-user address modify/delete with ownership reassignment is High (delivery interception path). `GET /rest/admin/application-configuration` unauth dump verified but contains no secrets — informational only.
